purpose: Approved question bank for MediKiosk AI-guided patient intake. Questions collect information for clinician review and must not be used as diagnosis or treatment instructions.
usage_rules: Ask one primary question at a time.
Prefer questions relevant to the patient's complaint and unanswered fields.
Do not ask every question in a category.
Never invent a question-specific patient answer.
Preserve the patient's original wording separately from normalized data.
Potential emergency signals are handed to the safety/rules engine; the AI intake agent does not make the final escalation decision.
If a patient refuses a question, record declined and continue when safe and appropriate.
Use simple language and match the patient's language where possible.

global_questions.question: Is it okay if I ask you a few questions about your health before you see the doctor?
How long have you been experiencing this?
Did it start suddenly or gradually?
How severe is it from 0 to 10?
Is it getting better, getting worse, or staying about the same?
Do you have any existing medical conditions that may be relevant?
Are you currently taking any regular medicines or supplements?
Do you have any known medicine, food, or other allergies?
Have you already seen a doctor or received any treatment for this problem?
Is there anything else about this problem that you think the doctor should know?

respiratory.description: Use when the main complaint involves cough, breathing, congestion, wheezing, or related respiratory symptoms.

questions.question: Do you have a cough?
How long have you had the cough?
Is the cough dry or does it bring up mucus?
Are you having any difficulty breathing?
Have you noticed wheezing or a whistling sound when breathing?
Have you had a fever or felt unusually hot or cold?
If you are bringing up mucus, what does it look like?

chest.description: Use when the patient reports chest pain, pressure, tightness, or discomfort.

questions.question: Where exactly do you feel the chest discomfort?
How would you describe the discomfort, such as pressure, tightness, burning, or pain?
How long does each episode of chest discomfort last?
Does it happen or get worse with physical activity?
Do you have any difficulty breathing along with the chest discomfort?
Have you felt dizzy, faint, or unusually weak with it?
Does the discomfort spread to another area, such as your arm, shoulder, back, neck, or jaw?

fever.description: Use when fever or elevated temperature is a main concern.

questions.question: How long have you had the fever or feverish feeling?
If you measured your temperature, what was the highest reading?
Have you had chills or shivering?
What other symptoms are happening with the fever?

gastrointestinal.description: Use for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, or related complaints.

questions.question: Where in your abdomen do you feel the problem?
How would you describe the abdominal pain?
Are you feeling nauseated?
Have you been vomiting?
Have you had loose or watery stools?
Have you been having difficulty passing stool?
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?

headache_neurological.description: Use for headache, dizziness, weakness, numbness, or other neurological complaints.

questions.question: Where do you feel the headache or other discomfort?
Did the headache or symptom begin suddenly or gradually?
Have you been feeling dizzy or off balance?
Have you noticed any new changes in your vision?
Have you noticed any new weakness or numbness?
Have you noticed any new difficulty speaking or understanding speech?

musculoskeletal.description: Use for joint, muscle, bone, back, neck, or injury-related complaints.

questions.question: Where exactly is the pain or discomfort?
Did this start after an injury, fall, or accident?
Is there any swelling in the area?
Does movement make it worse or limit your movement?
Is it affecting your ability to walk, use the limb, or perform normal activities?

urinary.description: Use for urinary discomfort, frequency, changes in urination, or related complaints.

questions.question: Do you have pain or burning when urinating?
Have you been urinating more often than usual?
Have you noticed any blood or an unusual change in the urine?
Are you having pain in your lower abdomen, side, or back along with the urinary symptoms?

skin.description: Use for rash, itching, skin lesions, swelling, or skin changes.

questions.question: Where on your body is the skin change?
When did you first notice it?
Is it itchy, painful, or neither?
Has it been spreading or changing?
Have you used any new medicine, food, product, or substance around the time it started?

general_health.description: Use when the complaint is vague or includes fatigue, weakness, or general symptoms.

questions.question: Have you been feeling unusually tired or weak?
Have you noticed an unexpected change in your weight recently?
Have your symptoms been affecting your sleep?
Are these symptoms affecting your usual daily activities?

priority_order: Information needed to understand the complaint
selection_logic: First use information already provided by the patient.
Identify the complaint category or categories.
Check required fields that remain missing.
Check relevant category questions that remain unanswered.
Prefer the question that reduces the most important information gap.
Do not ask irrelevant category questions.
If a potential safety signal is detected, stop normal questioning and hand the signal to the safety/rules engine.
Do not let the LLM invent clinical rules.
